name: Nationalpark Hohe Tauern
kurzbeschreibung: Hohe Tauern National Park is the largest nature reserve in the Alps: 3,000 m giants, the Pasterze Glacier, thunderous cascades, and alpine ibex.
beschreibung:
Overview

The majestic Hohe Tauern National Park stands as the largest and most storied nature reserve in Austria and the entire alpine region. Spanning an immense area of over 1,856 square kilometers, this extraordinary protected territory extends across the three Austrian provinces of Tyrol (East Tyrol), Salzburg, and Carinthia. The reserve encompasses the high-alpine crest of the Central Alps and is home to more than three hundred summits surpassing three thousand meters, including Austria's two highest peaks: the iconic Grossglockner (3,798 m) and the glaciated Grossvenediger (3,657 m). Vast glaciers like the Pasterze, roaring cascades such as the Krimml and Umbal Waterfalls, and ancient stone-pine forests characterize this alpine wilderness. The park provides vital sanctuary for rare wildlife including golden eagles, bearded vultures, chamois, and re-established alpine ibex.

Route & Requirements

The national park offers an endless network of trails catering to every generation and skill level. Families and casual walkers can explore dozens of easy educational and thematic paths, such as the water experience trail at the Umbal Waterfalls in Prägraten or the barrier-free glacier trail in scenic Innergschlöss near Matrei, widely hailed as the most beautiful valley head in the Alps. Seasoned alpinists can tackle renowned long-distance trails like the Venediger High Trail or participate in guided high-alpine treks led by certified park rangers. Rapid weather shifts in this high-altitude realm require sturdy waterproof boots, thermal layers, and reliable sun protection in every backpack. To safeguard fragile flora and fauna, staying on designated paths and keeping dogs on a leash is mandatory.

Visit & Arrival

The national park is easily accessed via well-connected routes from all directions. Key gateway towns in East Tyrol include Matrei, Kals am Grossglockner, and Prägraten am Grossvenediger, all conveniently linked to the B108 Felbertauern highway. Rail travellers alight at Lienz and board regular regional buses into the park valleys. The National Park House in Matrei offers multimedia exhibitions year-round.

Tips

Join a guided ranger tour through the Gschlösstal valley to observe wild alpine ibex and soaring bearded vultures through high-powered spotting scopes. Visiting the National Park House in Matrei provides fascinating insights into glaciology and local ecology.
preis: National park territory and theme trails freely accessible; visitor centre exhibits apply fees
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; prime mountaineering season from June to October
